exact_statement: For arbitrary Boolean a,b on a finite uniform core cube, m>=1, t=2^(-2m), and F=q2G with paired cores (a,b,-b,-a) indexed by c+2u, q2 negative on c=0,Z=0, fix one positive common core reference and the five-cell law (1/4,1/4,1/16,7/20,7/80). In every adaptive physical core-only tree with distinct queries per path, carry the common reference by frequency marginalization and retain the actual flag prior. With d_v=Pr(a!=b|v), p_v the physical node probability, and J_v=h2(t d_v)-E_child h2(t d_child), the total expected flag decrement equals h2(t d_root)-E_leaf h2(t d_leaf) and is at most t h2(d_root)<=t, independent of depth. Consequently total positive complete-reference query excess over K times queried influence is at most total positive core-reference excess plus t h2(d_root). All terminal reference costs and prior debits remain. For the fixed Maj3/y0 cores and inherited R=(8/13,2/13,1/26,...,1/26), preserving the signed core prices yields 4I(F)-C_Q(F)>9/4 for all m>=1. No arbitrary-core payment of the retained positive excess or universal FEI theorem is asserted.

In bits, put A=(I(a)+I(b))/2 and B=(C_R(a)+C_R(b))/2. The complete actual reference obeys C_Q(F)<B+4I_controls(F)-3/4; hence B<=K A, K>=0 implies H(F)<=C_Q(F)<max(K,4)I(F)-3/4, without a depth bound. For the specific nine-bit a=Maj3(Maj3(Y0,Y1,Y2),Maj3(Y3,Y4,Y5),Maj3(Y6,Y7,Y8)), b=a with only input0 flipped, R(S)=2^-L(S)/(6959/8192), L(S)=1+3[1{S nonempty}+sum_{j=0,3,6}1{S meets block j..j+2}], use physical order Y0,...,Y8, all actual outcomes and inherited frequency marginals at K4. The cumulative expected positive core excess is<7/12 and the single flag bill is<1/128. The original first physical child Y0=0 has complete surplus>5/4 uniformly in m and original weight1/2. One5/8 reserve owned exclusively by that child pays EVERY cumulative positive complete query excess in this fixed tree, including the root and all old debits, with total spend<3/5 and unused remainder>1/40 at every chronological prefix. Both full child reference costs remain. At the root and depth2 prefix0 the actual bad query has both child core pairs nonconstant; depth5 has a constant child core pair and is included with its full bill. This is an expected-tree bank allocation, not a pathwise bound or an arbitrary-core/history payment theorem. No universally paid common reference or full FEI result is asserted.
